# Case Study: Why We Killed a Profitable Product (The BrilliantHost Story)

Most case studies brag about what a team built. This one is about what we built, and what we chose to walk away from.

BrilliantHost was a VPS hosting product we built, launched, and scaled under the traztech brand. In under three months it hit 250 paying customers and $13K MRR. It was profitable. It was growing. And we shut it down on purpose.

If you are a founder or CTO trying to figure out whether a team can actually ship, and whether they have the discipline to make hard calls, that is the story worth telling.

## What we built

BrilliantHost was VPS hosting for businesses and individuals. Not a reseller play. Not a thin wrapper over someone else's cloud. We built and managed our own infrastructure: physical servers, network, the whole stack.

Everything around it was ours too:

- Product development and the customer-facing platform
- Provisioning, monitoring, and operations
- Billing and account management
- Marketing and sales
- Customer support

The traztech team, small, senior, and tightly coordinated, owned every layer of it. Our founder led the build, and we ran it the way we run client engagements: end-to-end, no hand-offs, no excuses.

## The results

- 250 customers acquired
- $13K MRR at peak
- Under 3 months from launch to that number

# I shut down a product with 200 paying customers. · 2026-07-01T00:00:00+00:00

I shut down a product with 200 paying customers.
Here's why:
It was making $4K MRR.
Growing slowly.
Customers were happy.
But every morning I dreaded opening the laptop.
The product was in a niche I didn't care about.
The support tickets bored me.
The roadmap felt like a chore list.
I kept telling myself: "It's making money, just push through."
Six months in, I was burned out, building nothing new, losing customers I didn't replace.
So I gave existing customers 90 days notice, refunded annual plans, and shut it down.
The lesson:
Money isn't enough of a reason.
Not when you're solo.
Not when the work is the work for the next 5 years.
If you don't care about the problem, no amount of revenue will save you.
Pick something you'd still work on if it was making half what you make now.

# I'm Shutting Down Content Goblin - A Post Mortem

I've made the difficult decision to shut down my SaaS Content Goblin. It's no longer financially viable for me to keep running the software.

Content Goblin was my tool to generate image based listicles, recipes, and Pinterest pins for the articles.

## Why I created Content Goblin

For about 25 years I've been into creating and monetizing websites and content. I've run affiliate ad campaigns, built content based websites monetized with ads, and software.

In 2024, I started to dive into Pinterest monetization. Pinterest was growing fast and sending massive amounts of traffic to publisher websites.

The basic model was:

- Create a listicle
- Pin a bunch of pins to Pinterest
- Send traffic to your website
- Monetize via display ads

I found was having a hard time keeping up with the posting volume necessary to keep traffic coming to the website regularly. Then I discovered a tool called Pin Generator that helped me schedule the pins in bulk, but I still had to manually create the articles.

So I started making my own scripts to help with the article generation part. Initially it was a fairly simple Jupyter notebook that evolved into a web UI.
